title: Installer — plan 001
epic_title: Ship the Pyxis installer: the system release, the pyxis orchestrator, and converge

tasks.title: Parse and derive the release manifest from the authored class policy
tasks.goal: the release-manifest and class-policy contracts exist as one closed-parse Go library, and a payload tree walks into a derived manifest or fails by name.
tasks.current: no manifest or class-policy schema exists anywhere; the only release metadata is a SHA256SUMS file for one tool.
tasks.desired: the library closed-parses `class-policy/v1` and `release-manifest/v1` (unknown keys are errors); a walk over a payload tree against the policy produces the manifest object (per-file sha256 + ownership class, per-binary per-platform hashes, system version, source commit); a payload file no policy glob matches fails the walk naming the file; the source repo's authored class-policy file lands with the library.
scope: The two closed schemas with golden fixtures, additive-evolution-ready.
The policy walk (first-match-wins globs, three ownership classes) and its unclassed-file refusal.
The authored class-policy data file for the current payload tree.
out_of_scope: The release workflow that calls the walk (T11); converge's consumption of the manifest (T5).
acceptance: Golden manifest fixtures round-trip byte-stable; unknown keys in either schema are named defects.
A fixture payload with one unclassed file fails the walk naming exactly that file.
The walk over the real payload tree with the authored policy classes every file (no unclassed remainder).
key_interfaces: `relmanifest.Manifest`, `relmanifest.ClassPolicy`, `relmanifest.Walk(payloadRoot, policy) (Manifest, error)`; ownership-class enum (engine-verbatim · repo-owned · generated).
touches: internal/relmanifest/ (new) · the system tree's authored class-policy data file (new)

tasks.title: Extend the repo config to schema v2 with the dual-read window
tasks.goal: the one operand config surface speaks schema v2 — system pin pair, knobs, branch, captured paths with the closure rule, epoch, artifact-source override — while dual-reading today's per-tool pin sections with a deprecation surface.
tasks.current: the config parser reads per-tool pin sections (docgate, codegate), paths, and plan thresholds; no schema-version field, no knobs, no epoch, no system pins.
tasks.desired: schema v2 closed-parses the new blocks; legacy per-tool pin sections still parse during the window and surface a deprecation notice through the doctor seam; a config carrying pin keys beyond the system pair — or legacy sections once the window closes — refuses by name; every captured path key enforces refuse-non-default; a conformance test asserts no engine configurable-path read lacks a schema key.
scope: The v2 schema blocks and their closed parse.
The dual-read of legacy pin sections plus the deprecation surface.
The refuse-non-default posture per path key and the path-closure conformance test.
out_of_scope: Flipping the source repo's own config (T12); any consumer behavior change behind the unchanged defaults.
acceptance: v2 fixtures parse; unknown keys, extra pin keys, and post-window legacy sections each refuse by name.
Every non-default path-key fixture refuses with the not-yet-configurable error; zero silent-ignore paths in the conformance sweep.
Existing suites pass unchanged with the new schema present (defaults change no behavior).
key_interfaces: `config.SchemaVersion`, `config.System{Version, ManifestSHA256, ArtifactSource, Mode}`, `config.Knobs`, `config.Epoch`; the path-closure conformance test.
touches: internal/docgate/config/ (extend) · the system config file (schema fields only; the source repo's mode flip is T12)

tasks.title: The acquisition core: fetch-verify-cache with per-exec re-hash
tasks.goal: one Go implementation owns every step from config pin to verified execution: manifest fetch-verify-cache, binary fetch-verify-cache, per-exec re-hash, override, source-mode fall-through, and the cache janitor.
tasks.current: resolution lives in per-tool shell scripts; one verifies against a pin, two verify nothing; no manifest exists.
tasks.desired: resolution reads the config pin → verifies the cached manifest (fetching on miss) → resolves the tool's platform hash → re-hashes the cached binary before every execution → fetch-verifies on miss or mismatch (tmp + atomic rename, artifact-source-override-aware) → refuses by name when offline or tampered; source mode falls through to source execution only where the source tree exists; a pre-warm entry fetches the full tool set; the janitor removes cached entries whose version is off the pin.
scope: The resolve → verify → exec decision function and its cache lifecycle (manifest + binaries + janitor).
Tamper, truncation, wrong-platform, missing-pin, and offline-miss refusals, each named.
The override and source-mode legs.
out_of_scope: The `pyxis` verb surface that fronts this (T4); converge's orchestration of pre-warm (T5).
acceptance: Tampered manifest, tampered binary, and truncated-fetch fixtures each refuse with zero execution, naming expected vs actual.
A cold cache self-heals online via a file:// fixture source; offline it refuses naming the pre-warm remedy; a second resolve of a warm tool performs no fetch.
After a pin bump plus pre-warm, off-version cache entries are gone; the override fixture fetches from the alternate source under the same verification.
key_interfaces: `resolve.Tool(ctx, cfg, tool, platform) (execPath, error)`, `resolve.PreWarm(ctx, cfg)`, `resolve.Reap(cfg)`; the manifest-cache location contract from the solution shape.

tasks.title: The pyxis binary: verbs, the exec grammar, and the fail-closed parser
tasks.goal: the `pyxis` thin main exists with the frozen verb surface, the I3-fail-closed argument discipline on every verb, and `pyxis exec <tool> -- <argv>` delegating through the acquisition core.
tasks.current: no `pyxis` binary; tools are invoked directly or through shell resolvers.
tasks.desired: the main dispatches the init, converge, repair, doctor, exec, and version verbs; a flag-like token in a positional slot, an unknown flag, or a missing `--` on exec refuses with a usage error before any write or external operation, via one shared guard; everything after `--` passes argv-verbatim to the resolved tool; exec's exit code is the tool's; the init, converge, and doctor verbs delegate to their libraries as those land.
scope: The verb dispatch and the shared fail-closed parse guard.
The exec grammar end to end over the acquisition core, source mode included.
Verb stubs that refuse-with-remedy until their libraries land (no silent no-ops).
out_of_scope: The behavior behind the init, converge, and doctor verbs (T5 through T8); any second entry binary.
acceptance: Misparse fixtures (flag-after-positional, unknown flag, missing `--`) on every verb refuse pre-action with zero writes and zero external operations.
`pyxis exec` runs a fixture tool argv-verbatim (bytes after `--` untouched) and propagates its exit code; in source mode it falls through to source execution.
The verbs spend zero model inference (structural: no inference call sites).
key_interfaces: The verb dispatch table; `parseArgs` (the shared guard); the exec grammar contract from the solution shape.

tasks.title: The converge engine: ownership classes, idempotency, preview
tasks.goal: one converge library reconciles a repo against the pinned manifest per ownership class, idempotently and raceably, with a preview mode that reports the exact write set and performs none of it.
tasks.current: no converge exists; the system tree arrives by being the source repo.
tasks.desired: engine-verbatim drift repairs byte-exact, generated files regenerate, repo-owned files validate against their closed schema and are never rewritten (violations named); a second run on a converged tree mutates nothing and reports convergence; an interrupted run re-runs to the identical end state; converge orchestrates the acquisition pre-warm and the cache janitor; `--preview` enumerates every write and external operation without performing any.
scope: The per-class reconcile over the manifest with one drift predicate.
Idempotency, kill-and-re-run convergence, and the preview write-set report.
Pre-warm plus janitor orchestration.
out_of_scope: Seeding and wiring (init's steps — T7/T8); doctor's read-only face (T6).
acceptance: Injected drift per class: engine-verbatim repaired byte-exact, generated regenerated, repo-owned schema-invalid refused by name with the file untouched.
A second converge run produces zero file mutations; kill-at-random-step fixtures all converge on re-run to the identical tree.
Preview output enumerates the exact write set of a subsequent real run; the preview run itself leaves the filesystem and remote state untouched.
key_interfaces: `converge.Run(ctx, cfg, manifest, opts) (Report, error)` with `opts.Preview`; the drift predicate shared with doctor; `converge.Report{Repaired, Regenerated, RefusedByName}`.

tasks.title: Doctor: the read-only drift and health face
tasks.goal: `pyxis doctor` reports manifest drift by ownership class and environment health with zero mutations.
tasks.current: no doctor verb exists anywhere in the toolset.
tasks.desired: doctor reads the same drift predicate as converge and names every divergence by class; reports environment health — Git present, gh present in GitHub mode, hooks active, tracker reachable, CLI surfaces intact; reports the epoch block, legacy-config deprecation notices, stale cache entries the janitor missed, and unauthored-skeleton advisories; a doctor run performs zero filesystem or remote mutations.
scope: The read-only report over the shared drift predicate.
The environment, epoch, deprecation, and advisory checks.
out_of_scope: Any repair action (converge owns mutation); wiring health beyond reachability.
acceptance: Each injected drift class and each removed prerequisite is detected and named; a clean install reports healthy.
The filesystem diff across a doctor run is empty and no external mutation is performed.
Unauthored governance skeletons and legacy pin sections each surface as named advisories.
key_interfaces: `converge.Doctor(ctx, cfg) (Health, error)`; the advisory taxonomy (drift · prerequisite · epoch · deprecation · skeleton).

tasks.title: Init core: target check, knobs, capture, epoch
tasks.goal: `pyxis init` runs the pipeline's front half: admit or refuse the target, elicit the five knobs (or take flags/answers), converge the payload, and capture config plus epoch.
tasks.current: no init path exists; a fresh repo fails the gates for lack of structure, config, and hooks.
tasks.desired: an empty target (no tracked content) is admitted — git-initialized where no repository exists; a non-empty or dirty target refuses before any write, enumerating conflicts; unset committer identity yields a repo-local identity from the answers or a named refusal, never a failed commit; the five knobs elicit interactively with recommended defaults or resolve entirely from flags/an answers file with zero prompts; every answer, path, pin, and the branch land in the v2 config; the epoch block writes once (system version, epoch commit, manifest hash); converge materializes the payload.
scope: Target admission (bare dir and git-initialized empty repo), refusals, and identity handling.
Knob elicitation with full flag/answers parity.
Config capture, the epoch write, and the converge invocation.
out_of_scope: Seeding, dependencies, hooks, wiring, welcome (T8); GitHub operations (T10).
acceptance: Init from a bare directory and from a git-initialized empty repo both produce the converged tree with a complete v2 config and epoch block; the two entry states end byte-identical.
Non-empty and dirty targets refuse before any write with the conflict set named; identity-unset fixtures produce a working repo-local identity or the named refusal with no failed-commit state.
The full flag/answers path completes with zero prompts; asked knobs are exactly the five.
key_interfaces: `installer.Init(ctx, opts) (Report, error)`; `installer.Answers` (the five knobs + flags parity); the epoch write contract.

tasks.title: Init tail: seeding, dependencies, hooks, wiring, welcome, green proof
tasks.goal: init ends green: skeletons and registries seeded from the self-contained payload, hooks active, tracker and CI wired per the knobs, the welcome path emitted, and the gate passing.
tasks.current: none of the end state exists; the manual steps (hook activation, store init) are documented one-time commands in the source repo only.
tasks.desired: the governance skeletons and the operand manual instantiate from the shipped templates (knob-substituted, repo-owned; zero invented governing content); registries create empty-but-valid; rollups stay absent; the argus knob off skips the authority-contract instantiable entirely; all runtime inputs come from the verified payload with no package-install step; hooks activate without manual steps and reject a violating commit; carina mode initializes the local store, GitHub mode walks the declared operation set, actions mode installs the payload workflow; the welcome item emits with authorship pointers; the gate exits green on the seeded tree.
scope: Seeding orchestration (instantiables, registries, argus-conditional suppression).
Verified-payload materialization and hook activation.
Tracker/CI wiring dispatch and the welcome emission plus the final gate proof.
out_of_scope: The GitHub operation implementations (T10); template content (T9).
acceptance: Post-init the gate exits green in every knob combination; seeded skeletons diff clean against their templates apart from knob substitutions.
With argus off no authority contract exists and the skill's refusal path is reachable; with argus on the floor-tier surface is instantiated.

The offline combo materializes the complete payload with zero network and no package install; hooks reject a gate-violating commit without any manual activation step; carina mode answers a store query post-init.
key_interfaces: The seeding orchestration over the instantiable set; the wiring dispatch (carina init · the operation table · workflow install); the green-proof invocation.

tasks.title: The shipped instantiables and the installed-repo workflow variant
tasks.goal: every artifact init instantiates ships in the payload: the four governance-doc skeletons, the operand agents manual, the welcome item template, and the installed-repo variant of the gate workflow.
tasks.current: no skeleton templates exist (a fresh repo fails the gates for their absence); the only gate workflow is the source repo's, which runs source-toolchain steps no installed repo can execute.
tasks.desired: the four skeletons carry template structure and fill-me guidance with zero invented governing content and pass the gate's structure checks when instantiated; the operand manual template carries the factory's operating rules with knob substitution points; the welcome template carries the authorship pointers and first-feature path; the installed-repo workflow variant invokes the gate through the exec grammar with zero source-toolchain steps.
scope: The six template files, substitution-point conventions consistent with the existing instantiable set.
The installed-repo workflow variant as payload content distinct from the source repo's own workflow.
out_of_scope: The instantiation engine (T8); the class-policy rows classing these files (T1's authored data grows in the same change they land).
acceptance: A fixture instantiation of the four skeletons plus registries passes the gate's structure checks with zero content beyond structure and guidance.
The installed workflow variant contains exec-grammar gate steps and zero source-toolchain steps (no Go setup, vet, or race suite).
The operand manual and welcome templates render with every knob substitution resolved for both tracker modes.
key_interfaces: The instantiable naming set from the solution shape; the substitution-variable convention.
touches: the system template set (new instantiables) · the payload home of the installed workflow variant

tasks.title: The wiring library: the operation table over the gh CLI
tasks.goal: GitHub wiring is one declared-operation table executed through the gh CLI, with preview, audit, permission hand-off, and transient retry.
tasks.current: no wiring exists; labels, protection, and workflows are hand-configured.
tasks.desired: the operation table (ensure-labels, push-workflow, set-protection, create-repo, welcome-item) is the single contract: preview renders it, execution walks exactly it via gh, the audit event records what ran; gh absent is a named GitHub-mode prerequisite failure; a missing permission completes every permitted operation and emits a copy-paste hand-off for the remainder, reporting partial; transient API failures retry within a stated bound then hand off; the executed set never exceeds the declared set.
scope: The operation table, its knob conditions, and the gh transport behind it.
Preview and audit from the same table; the hand-off and bounded-retry legs.
out_of_scope: When operations run (init's dispatch — T8); non-GitHub trackers.
acceptance: Against a fake gh transcript, the executed operation set equals the declared table in every knob combination; the audit event records it.
A permission-limited transcript yields the permitted subset applied plus a hand-off block that completes the remainder verbatim; a 429 transcript retries within the bound then hands off.
With gh absent, GitHub-mode wiring refuses with the named prerequisite remedy and zero operations.
key_interfaces: `wire.Table(cfg) []Op`, `wire.Execute(ctx, ops) (Audit, error)`, `wire.Preview(ops)`; the Op row shape from the solution shape.

tasks.title: The system release: one tag to a complete verified artifact set
tasks.goal: one version tag publishes the complete artifact set — every scan-derived binary per platform, the self-contained payload archive, the derived manifest, and checksums — re-runnably; and the bootstrap shim consumes it.
tasks.current: one tool has a tag-triggered release; no system payload, manifest, or bootstrap exists.
tasks.desired: the release workflow derives the binary list by command-tree scan, builds the platform matrix, packs the self-contained payload, derives the manifest via the policy walk, and publishes with checksums; publish is upload-or-verify (a re-run completes or byte-verifies, never forks); the build refuses to publish while any payload hook or workflow references a retired resolver, carries a source-toolchain step, or includes an undeclared file; the bootstrap shim fetch-verifies the pyxis binary against the pin documented in the install instructions, bash-3.2-clean, delegate-only, covered by a test.
scope: The release workflow with the scan-derived matrix and the three-artifact packing.
The release-precondition assertions and upload-or-verify publish.
The bootstrap shim and its test.
out_of_scope: Cutting the first live tag (an operator act after the plan's tasks land); channels or cohorts.
acceptance: A dry-run from a fixture tag yields the complete set (scan-derived binaries × platforms, self-contained payload, manifest, checksums) and a publish re-run converges upload-or-verify.
Precondition fixtures (a retired-resolver reference, a source-toolchain step in the payload workflow, a bundle/lockfile mismatch) each refuse publish by name.
The bootstrap shim on clean darwin/linux fixtures fetch-verifies pyxis against the documented pin and refuses a tampered binary with zero execution; the shim test passes on bash 3.2.
key_interfaces: The release workflow's job graph; the build-only manifest-derivation entry over `relmanifest.Walk`; the documented-pin convention the shim reads.
touches: .github/workflows/ (new system-release workflow) · the system scripts home (bootstrap shim) · cmd/ (build-only manifest entry over T1)

tasks.title: Migrate the source repo: delegates, schema flip, parity preserved
tasks.goal: the source repo consumes the new path itself: resolver scripts collapse to exec-grammar delegates, the config flips to schema v2 in source mode, and every source-repo suite stays green through the new path.
tasks.current: three per-tool resolver scripts carry their own fetch/parse logic (two verify nothing); hooks and skills invoke them directly; the config speaks the legacy per-tool schema.
tasks.desired: each resolver script is a one-line delegate into the exec grammar; hook shims and skill invocation lines speak the exec grammar; the config carries schema v2 with source mode, exercising the dual-read window's happy path; the full source-repo gate and test suite pass unchanged in verdict through the new invocation path.
scope: The delegate collapse and the invocation-line sweep across hooks and skills.
The source-repo config flip to v2 source mode.
out_of_scope: Deleting the dual-read window (a later release closes it per the design's Q-3); any behavior change in the tools themselves.
acceptance: Every former resolver call site reaches its tool through the exec grammar; no script carries fetch or parse logic beyond locate-and-delegate.
The full source-repo suite and gate are green with identical verdicts through the new path (the parity baseline for NR-1).
Doctor on the source repo reports source mode and zero deprecation notices post-flip.
key_interfaces: The exec-grammar invocation convention for hooks and skills; the source-mode config contract.
touches: the system scripts home (resolver scripts → delegates) · the system hooks (invocation lines) · the system config file (v2 flip
source mode) · the system skills (invocation-line sweep)

tasks.title: The e2e harness: local combos, failure drills, repair proof
tasks.goal: the scratch-repo e2e harness proves the local half of the matrix: offline and carina combos, converge repair, idempotency, kill/re-run, fresh-clone self-heal, and the misparse suite.
tasks.current: no installer e2e exists; nothing exercises the packaged layout outside the source repo.
tasks.desired: the harness creates scratch repos, runs flag-driven installs from a fixture artifact source, and asserts: the offline combo (carina + local CI) completes every enumerated behavior in a network-denied environment including bundle-offline dependency install; injected drift per class repairs or refuses per the converge contract and a second run is a no-op; kill-at-random-step re-runs converge; a fresh clone of an installed repo self-heals online and refuses by name offline; misparse fixtures refuse on every verb; the removal test leaves operand content intact.
scope: The scratch-repo harness and fixture artifact source.
The network-denied offline leg; the repair, idempotency, and kill legs; the fresh-clone and misparse legs; the removal test.
out_of_scope: GitHub-mode combos, wiring transcripts, parity, and budgets (T14).
acceptance: The offline combo passes in a network-denied environment with an egress scan showing zero operations post-fetch.
The drift matrix (per-class injections × repair/refuse × second-run no-op) and the kill/re-run fixtures all converge as contracted.
Fresh-clone, misparse, and removal-test legs pass on both linux and darwin runners.
key_interfaces: The harness's scratch-repo and fixture-source contracts; the drift-injection fixture set.

tasks.title: The matrix tail: GitHub combos, parity, drills, budgets
tasks.goal: the matrix completes: GitHub-mode combos through first-push green, the source-vs-installed parity suite, the supply-chain drills, and the time budgets.
tasks.current: the harness (T13) covers local combos only; no GitHub-mode, parity, drill, or budget evidence exists.
tasks.desired: GitHub-mode combos run the full wiring against a live scratch repo — labels, protection level, workflow — and the first push's required check completes green; the parity suite runs identical fixtures in the source repo (source mode) and an installed repo and diffs verdicts to zero divergence; the drill set (tampered binary, payload, manifest, bootstrap script; declared-operation audit) all refuse or verify as contracted; the install budget (≤ 5 min p95) and the per-invocation budget (≤ 100 ms p95) hold on reference runners, recorded.
scope: The GitHub-mode legs (wiring + first-push) and the parity suite.
The tamper-drill set and the two budget measurements.
out_of_scope: New harness machinery beyond T13's contracts; non-GitHub hosts.
acceptance: Every GitHub-mode combo ends with the wiring audit equal to the declared table and the first push's required check green.
The parity suite reports zero verdict divergence; the drill set refuses every tamper fixture with zero execution.
Recorded timings hold ≤ 5 min p95 install and ≤ 100 ms p95 per invocation across the matrix runs.
key_interfaces: The parity fixture contract; the drill fixture set; the timing-record format the matrix emits.
